picks.title: We have more details on Apple's camera-equipped AirPods, and they are pretty dang weird
picks.excerpt: Apple's camera-equipped AirPods will put a camera in each bud, capturing synchronized low-res stills — not video — that feed Visual Intelligence. On-device processing filters blurred or obstructed shots before anything is used.
picks.rationale: A camera that takes stills instead of video and discards its own bad frames is a new sensing pattern designers will have to build interfaces around.

picks.title: RayNeo splits its AR line with the camera-free iO and the cinema-scale GT series
picks.excerpt: RayNeo split its AR line in two directions at once: the lightweight, camera-free iO for all-day AI assistance and the heavier GT series built for cinema-scale viewing. Two opposite bets on what smart glasses are actually for.
picks.rationale: One vendor shipping two contradictory glasses at once is the clearest read yet on how unsettled the smart-glasses design brief still is.

picks.title: Meta patent might solve privacy concerns on smart glasses with a hardware lock
picks.excerpt: A new Meta patent proposes a physical 'hardware lock' for smart-glasses cameras, aimed at the severe backlash over always-on AI eyewear. It reframes privacy as an industrial-design problem rather than a settings screen.
picks.rationale: Moving consent from a toggle to a physical mechanism is the kind of decision that belongs to industrial design, not privacy policy.

picks.title: Proposed Oura lawsuit highlights the limits of wearable health tracking
picks.excerpt: A proposed class action claims Oura's smart rings overstate sleep-tracking accuracy because they lack brain and eye-movement sensors. The suit puts a legal price on how confidently AI health wearables present inferred data.
picks.rationale: How confidently you display an inferred number is now a legal question, which changes copy, charts and disclosure in every health UI.

picks.title: Google Home update improves Gemini voice controls for lighting and media
picks.excerpt: Gemini for Home's latest update finally handles specific kelvin color-temperature commands, better Spotify recognition and cleaner broadcasts. Small fixes that expose how much of AI smart-home UX is command-parsing craft.
picks.rationale: The gap between an assistant that works and one that annoys turns out to be a handful of parsing details, not a bigger model.
